title: What the offcuts are for
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Thursday. The mat offcuts go in a box. The owner says they're for nothing. Wood draws on one during lunch. She sees. She says that's what they're for. The box goes home with him Saturdays from now on.

panels.composition: A cardboard box under the cutting table: mat offcuts, cream, green, black, every width. WOOD's hand in it.

image.prompt: close on a box of mat board offcuts in cream, green and black beneath a cutting table with a young man's hand reaching in, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Lunch. Wood on the back step with a cream offcut and a pen. BARNABY. A drawing: the lot.

image.prompt: a young man on a shop's back step at lunch drawing on a piece of mat board with a pen, a small dog beside him, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The OWNER in the door behind him, looking at the drawing on the offcut.

balloons.text: You said they were for nothing.

image.prompt: a woman in reading glasses in a doorway looking down at a drawing on a piece of mat board, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Saturday's Datsun: the offcut box on the back seat beside the taped box of everything. Two boxes now. One's full of nothing, for something.

image.prompt: close on a car's back seat holding a taped cardboard box and a second box full of mat board scraps, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Two boxes on the back seat. The sums of April 20 were on an offcut already; now there's a supply.
